Services

Regular cuts, done right

The same services the shop has always offered, from its own published list. Tap one to see what it covers. Walk in for any of them.

Men's hairstyling and barbering: all regular cuts and styles, cut the way you ask for them.
A house specialty named in the shop's own description, leveled and squared off properly.
Beard trimming and shaping, on its own or alongside your cut.
A shampoo service at the bowl, the finishing touch to a cut.
Haircuts for senior citizens, a standing line on the shop's own price board.
Children's cuts too, per the shop's own description. First haircuts welcome.

Prices are posted on the board inside the shop. No appointments for any service: walk-ins only, first come, first seated.

The Shop

Period barbershop, kept as it should be

Burgundy Belmont chairs, gold-framed mirrors, walnut paneling, and a model-car case regulars have been looking at for years.

Since 1958

Three generations in the same plaza

The shop was founded in 1958 by Richard Beck and Judd Brouse, and it has been in the West Shore Plaza ever since. Duane Kennedy, Brouse's son-in-law, joined the family business in 1995 and has owned the shop since 2005. That makes it the third generation of the same family behind the chairs.

Duane cuts alongside John Haines, with the shop since about 2001, and Keith Husson, who joined about 2006. Regulars know the chairs, the chairs know the regulars, and Saturday mornings start early: the doors open at 5:30 AM for the walk-in crowd.
